subject: On‑prem cluster: node pool sizing, PV strategy, and rollout milestones
messages:
From: Sara Lim <sara.lim@edgeworks.io>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: On‑prem rollout: initial cluster requirements and constraints

Hi Jonas / Laura,

Thanks again for the PI demo last week — the team at EdgeWorks is keen to move to a proof‑of‑value (PoV) for a private deployment. Before we lock in dates, wanted to surface constraints from our infra side so the plan you send covers everything: 

- Two datacenters (primary and DR) with distinct L2 segments; east site preferred for primary.
- No public egress for inference hosts; control plane comms must be outbound TLS over a customer proxy.
- Existing storage arrays present: NetApp (primary) and Ceph (DR); we can present CSI endpoints.
- Expected steady QPS: 200 concurrent small‑prompt sessions, peak bursts up to 600 for batch windows.
- Desired RPO for models/cache: <5s for cache warmups; persist model artifacts to on‑prem object store nightly.

Can you sketch the node‑pool sizing and PV strategy we should plan for the PoV (2‑week window)? Also call out any network ports, proxy config, and required credentials for the control plane.

Thanks — Sara
Sara Lim
Head of Platform Engineering | EdgeWorks Inc.

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@edgeworks.io>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: On‑prem rollout: initial cluster requirements and constraints

Hi Sara — great summary, thanks.

We can definitely scope a PoV that meets those constraints. At a high level:

- Cluster topology: two clusters (primary + DR) with identical control plane configs; inference workloads pinned to primary for low latency, DR activated for failover.
- Node pools: a) small nodes (4 vCPU/16GB) for control plane and lightweight services; b) mid nodes (16 vCPU, 64GB) for API frontends and batching; c) GPU nodes (A100‑like or customer equivalent; 80GB vram class) for model inference + quantized model variants.
- Storage: use PVCs backed by NetApp for low latency model artifacts, mirrored to Ceph for DR. We'll provide CSI recommendations and a sample StorageClass.
- Networking: outbound TLS to our control plane via your proxy (we'll provide FQDNs + cert fingerprint). No inbound ports required beyond intra‑cluster.

I'll loop Marcus and Dev on a request for more granular sizing & an initial PV policy. Can you share typical prompt lengths and payload sizes so we can estimate KV cache sizing?

Next step: Marcus to propose node counts for the PoV by EOD tomorrow; we'll attach a draft diagram and PV policy for you to review.

— Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: marcus.lin@redwood.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Lim <sara.lim@edgeworks.io>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 08:15:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: On‑prem rollout: initial cluster requirements and constraints

Quick technical draft for PoV node counts based on the 200 steady / 600 burst (assumes batching improvements in Redwood runtime):

Assumptions:
- Average prompt length ~350 tokens; average response ~150 tokens.
- Baseline per‑token compute (quantized) approximated for 13B model at 0.8ms/token on target GPU.

PoV node pools (primary site):
- control-pool: 3 x m4.large (4vCPU/16GB) — kube control plane addons, ingress, logging.
- frontend-pool: 4 x m8.xlarge (16vCPU/64GB) — API proxy, batching worker, embedding workers.
- inference-gpu-pool: 3 x gpu‑80GB (80GB HBM) — each node can host 6 concurrent sessions (prefetch/KV) or 18 low‑priority batched requests.

This gives steady capacity comfortably above 200 concurrent sessions and headroom for scaling to 600 with burst autoscaling (scale inference pool to 6 nodes).

PV strategy:
- Model artifacts: RWMany PVs via NetApp CSI with a StorageClass 'netapp-fast' — mount models on inference nodes read‑only after model sync.
- KV cache: use ephemeral local volumes (emptyDir) for hot KV; persist checkpoints to a nightly snapshot to NetApp.
- Logs & metrics: forward to central ELK/Prometheus; short‑term local buffering (PVC) in case of network outages.

Network ports / proxy:
- Outbound: 443 to control.redwood.ai (and a secondary fallback host).
- mTLS optional for agent; we recommend client certs managed by your CA.

I'll attach a draft topology (PDF) and a sample pv policy YAML. Dev — can you add notes about kubelet volume limits & recommended ulimits for inference processes?

— Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: edgeworks-k8s-nodeplan-v1.pdf, pv-policy-examples.yaml
From: dev_patel@redwood.com
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Sara Lim <sara.lim@edgeworks.io>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 13:41:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: On‑prem rollout: initial cluster requirements and constraints

Couple of infra notes from DevOps perspective:

- kubelet volume limits: ensure host has at least 1.5x the model working set as free memory; for large models we recommend node memory >= model size + 80GB headroom.
- device plugin: use our vetted NVIDIA device plugin with exclusive‑process mode; pin GPUs via nodeAffinity and taints/tolerations for inference workloads.
- persistent volumes: set reclaimPolicy: Retain for model PVs during PoV; snapshot schedule nightly to your object store (S3‑compatible endpoint).
- QoS & throttling: apply ResourceQuotas per namespace and a LimitRange on inference pods to protect control plane.

I also included a sample sysctl and ulimit snippet in pv-policy-examples.yaml — important for mmap and file descriptors.

— Dev
Platform Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks team — this is helpful. A few clarifications from SRE: 

- Prompt length: commonly between 200–450 tokens; occasional long‑form payloads up to 2k tokens for batch jobs.
- Storage: NetApp team can expose NFS4 CSI with RWMany, and Ceph RGW for object snapshots.
- Timeline constraint: PoV kickoff week of Dec 13; we'd like a deploy checklist and a runbook for failover testing by Dec 10.

Can you provide the checklist and a short runbook for DR testing? Also confirm the IPs/FQDNs you need whitelisted and the format for the client certs.

— Sara
